caption: Focus on a single cell to find all possible tiles.
content: The basic technique for completing an Area is to @b{focus on a single cell}.

items: If there is only one tile that can be placed on a cell, you must place that tile.
If there is no tile that can be placed on a cell, you can't complete that Area.

content.caption: Example 1
content: Assuming your available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} @t{forest_road.2t.dl} @t{forest_road.2t.ul} @t{forest_road.2t.ur}, let's solve this Area.

For example, let's focus on the cell @m{pending}. On this cell, you can place road tiles that connect to the left: @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dl} @t{forest_road.2t.ul}. However, it's not yet clear which of the three we should place.
On the other hand, if we focus on the cell @m{satisfied}, the only tile that can be placed here is @t{forest_road.2t.ur}. Therefore, we have to place @t{forest_road.2t.ur} here.
Placing one tile narrows the candidates for the cell @m{pending} we focused on earlier. Now only @t{forest_road.2t.dl} can be placed here, so we place that tile.
By repeating this process, you can lay out the tiles like this and complete the Area.
